name: Arlington
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Arlington, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Arlington, MA: First Lights in Whittemore Park, Santa story time at the Holiday Market and the Arlington Heights Holiday Stroll.
lede: Arlington spreads Christmas along Massachusetts Avenue, from First Lights in Whittemore Park and Santa reading stories at the Holiday Market in Arlington Center to the painted windows and tree lighting of the Arlington Heights Holiday Stroll.
celebrates: Arlington's holiday season runs along Massachusetts Avenue. In Arlington Center, the Arlington Chamber of Commerce and the Cyrus Dallin Art Museum hold First Lights in Whittemore Park on the first Thursday of December, lighting the park and the Jefferson Cutter House with Santa, an ice sculptor and an art hunt in the museum. Arlington Brewing Company and the Chamber run the Arlington Holiday Market with more than 100 vendors and story time with Santa. Up the avenue, the Arlington Heights Community Association hosts its Holiday Stroll and Tree Lighting, with storefront windows painted by residents, a Touch-A-Truck, a puppet show and Santa photos at ACMi.
lastyear: In 2025 the Arlington Heights Community Association presented its fifth annual Holiday Stroll and Tree Lighting on Saturday, December 13, from 2 to 5 pm. Visitors walked Massachusetts Avenue from Shattuck Heights Hardware to Maruichi Japanese Food and Deli past more than 60 winter windows painted by residents in 25 storefronts. The afternoon included a Touch-A-Truck at the Heights Bus Depot, a Margaret Moody puppet show, a kids winter craft, a photo with Santa and holiday music.
facts: Arlington was known as Menotomy at the time of the Revolution, was incorporated as West Cambridge in 1807 and took the name Arlington in 1867. The Cyrus Dallin Art Museum, a host of First Lights, sits in the Jefferson Cutter House in Whittemore Park. The Arlington Heights stroll began in 2021, and in 2023 the Heights celebrated its third annual stroll and tree lighting.
trains: Arlington has no commuter rail station, but its rail history is easy to find. The Minuteman Bikeway follows the former Lexington Branch of the Boston and Maine Railroad through Arlington, and a piece of the original track can be seen near Uncle Sam Plaza in front of the Cyrus Dallin Art Museum. The bikeway ends at Alewife station on the Red Line in Cambridge. Farther afield, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train through the Christmas lights.

kidfact: Before it was called Arlington, the town had two other names: Menotomy and then West Cambridge. You can still see a piece of old railroad track on the bike path in front of the Cyrus Dallin Art Museum.
faq: What is First Lights in Arlington?

First Lights in Whittemore Park is Arlington Center's holiday lighting, presented by the Arlington Chamber of Commerce and the Cyrus Dallin Art Museum on the first Thursday of December. Families meet Santa, watch an ice sculptor, follow an art hunt in the museum, warm up in an igloo and sing along as the park's trees light up.
When is the Arlington Heights Holiday Stroll?

The stroll is held on a Saturday afternoon in mid-December from 2 to 5 pm, rain or shine, and ends with a tree lighting in front of ACMi on Park Avenue. In 2025 it was the fifth annual stroll, on December 13, with more than 60 painted windows along Massachusetts Avenue.
Where can kids see Santa in Arlington?

Santa appears at First Lights in Whittemore Park, reads stories at the Arlington Holiday Market in Arlington Center and poses for studio photos at ACMi during the Arlington Heights Holiday Stroll. All three are listed as free by their hosts or by the Arlington Chamber of Commerce.
Is there a train to Arlington?

Arlington has no commuter rail stop. The nearest rapid transit is Alewife station on the Red Line in Cambridge, where the Minuteman Bikeway begins. The bikeway runs through Arlington on the former Lexington Branch of the Boston and Maine Railroad, so families can walk or bike the old rail line.
